data.name: Dilwar
data.gender_notes: Dilwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who brings delight and joy to the heart, a warrior or protector. The name Dilwar carries the meaning “Delight of the Heart” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Dilwar usually hope their child will grow to embody delight of the heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who embody the warrior spirit and protect the hearts of those they love
data.etymology: Dilwar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delight of the Heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dilwar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dilwar in Hindu culture signifies a person who is a source of happiness and joy to those around them. This name is often given to a child who brings a smile to their parents' faces, or who has a naturally joyful and delightful disposition. It also speaks to the importance of courage and protection in Hindu society, as the word "warrior" implies strength, valor, and the ability to defend and secure the wellbeing of loved ones and community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Dilwar carries the deeper meaning of being a vessel of joy and bliss that uplifts the spirit of others. This name can serve as a reminder for the individual to always strive to bring happiness into their own world and the world of those around them. Additionally, the name may carry the importance of protection as a spiritual calling - being a protector of the divine within oneself and others, and embodying the qualities of a spiritual warrior.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dilwar in Hinduism symbolizes a pure and devoted heart (dil) that shines brightly (war), illuminated by the inner light of spiritual wisdom and selfless love for the divine. It is a reminder to keep the heart open and receptive to the divine grace and inner wisdom.

historical_references.reference: In the 13th century, there was a Hindu king named Dilwar who ruled over the Malwa region in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India. He was a powerful monarch who was known for his military prowess and his patronage of art and culture.

Another notable Hindu figure with the name Dilwar was a 16th-century Sikh guru who was the fourth guru in the Sikh lineage. Guru Ram Das, who was known as Dilwar Dayal, is revered in Sikhism for his wisdom, compassion, and his contribution to the Sikh community. He is best remembered for laying the foundation of the holy city of Amritsar and establishing the Harmandir Sahib, which is now the revered Golden Temple.
